anchors: Plans/LSPSupport.md#section=FABLE Deferred Action Concrete Repair Addendum - 2026-07-08
original.evidence: Jared settled the client foundation Plans/Decision_Log.md:63378 “Puppet Master builds its own client on the LSPSupport §3.6.1 stack”. The architecture permits Plans/LSPSupport.md:232 “`async-lsp` permitted only as an internal `/wire` helper if it fits PM's supervisor/session model”. The prerequisite now says Plans/LSPSupport.md:871 “Build PM's own stdio-capable client on the §3.6.1 baseline stack” and Plans/LSPSupport.md:871 “lsp-client and async_lsp_client are rejected alternatives, not dependencies”. LSPS-075 carries the same implementation prerequisite. The addendum expressly supersedes its contrary Phase 1 sentence Plans/LSPSupport.md:7059 “the sentence above overstated the choice and is withdrawn.”

The public response owner says Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:322 “These six strings are the only `disabled_reason` values a `capabilities.get` response carries.” The ten lowercase values have a different owner Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6724 “these ten lowercase values are the closed vocabulary of the `generated_media_route.disabled_reason` column above”. The table maps every row value, including Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6729 “`unsupported` | `BACKEND_UNSUPPORTED`” and Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6731 “`capability_gated` | `NOT_CONFIGURED`”. It also resolves route_unverified by active backend and sources RATE_LIMITED from live provider state. AC-MED05 makes the distinction explicit Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:1023 “`UNSUPPORTED` and `CAPABILITY_GATED` name the route row's `support_state` values `unsupported` and `capability_gated`”.

Settings dispatches Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6696 “`cmd.media.route.verify` from that exact row through `handlers::media::verify_route`”. Each image probe uses Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6702 “`count = 1`, the smallest size the route accepts” and Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6706 “A plain red circle centered on a white background” on that row's provider, account and model. Passing requires Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6712 “`success = true`, `engine.generated_media_route_id` equal to the probed `route_id`” and durable bytes with matching SHA-256, allowed MIME and positive decoded dimensions. The proof record includes Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6714 “`artifact_sha256` (string or null), `artifact_w` and `artifact_h` (integer or null)” plus route identity, snapshot, credential epoch, outcome and times. Cache expiry is Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6716 “`cache_expires_at_utc = verified_at_utc + 7 days`”. Only a passed human Verify renews it. A changed credential or provider capability epoch, a changed or no longer dispatchable model, or a definitive unsupported/unavailable result can invalidate it before expiry. DL-2602 specifies Plans/Decision_Log.md:63387 “a checked image-generation route stays trusted for 7 days and is re-checked only when the user asks”.

The admission rule is Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:6764 “Ordinary Cursor image generation requires a `generated_media_route` row for Cursor with `support_state = verified` and current image proof.” MGAC-061, MGAC-069 and MGAC-070 agree, including Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:4938 “Valid Gemini Direct or other provider credentials do not make Cursor a generated-media backend”. The existing image-only message is restricted to a backend with current image proof when Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:971 “it has no `verified` row whose output mode is `video` or `audio`” and the disabled kind is video, TTS or music. For an eligible unverified row the copy says Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:972 “The current backend has no verified generated-media route for this kind.” and offers Settings Verify. Without a probe-eligible row, Plans/Media_Generation_and_Capabilities.md:976 “the message names no verify action”. MGAC-066 records the same three variants.

Usage now routes each former number to its subject, including Plans/usage-feature.md:864 “grid, sizes and gestures (WS-017, WS-019), hostability (`#section=2. Hostability and data contracts`), widget catalogue and add-widget flow (WS-030), layout persistence (`#section=3. Layout persistence`, WS-020), widget configuration (WS-004)”. The operative per-widget text says Plans/usage-feature.md:823 “each settled layout record carries `configuration_refs`” and points to WS-020, WS-004, §3 and the board envelope in WS-030. The Widget owner explicitly maps Plans/Widget_System.md:1219 “`§7` and `#5` (widget configuration persistence) to `## 3. Layout persistence` with WS-020's `configuration_refs` and WS-004's configuration record”. These targets resolve at this revision.

W-050 now says Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md:3653 “Conflict worktree persistence is durable from the initial release: each unresolved merge conflict requires a typed worktree_conflict_state.v1:{project_id}:{worktree_id} row.” Section 7.4 says Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md:642 “only verified resolution or explicit discard” clears that row. Sections 2.3 and 7.14(3) adopt the same release rule. W-050 makes the former memory option explicit Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md:3653 “An in-memory HashSet<node_id> is a per-session projection of those rows and never the authority.” The persistence decision is settled. Enabling it still requires canonical storage registration Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md:643 “The storage owner must register the key, schema and conflict-preserving write, clear and recovery behavior before the initial release can enable this path.”
